description: A biotechnology company has 35,000 units of antibiotics available which is important to the process of making a first-dose and second-dose of vaccines. The first-dose vaccine requires 30 units of antibiotics and 20 mg of gelatine whereas the second-dose vaccine requires 65 units of antibiotics and 60 mg of gelatine. Since the first-dose vaccine is required before the second-dose vaccine, there must be more first-dose than second-dose vaccines manufactured. However, at least 40 second-dose vaccines must be made. How many of each vaccine should be made to minimize the amount of gelatine used?

AntibioticsFirstDose.definition: Antibiotics required for one first-dose vaccine

GelatineFirstDose.definition: Gelatine required for one first-dose vaccine

AntibioticsSecondDose.definition: Antibiotics required for one second-dose vaccine

GelatineSecondDose.definition: Gelatine required for one second-dose vaccine

MinimumSecondDose.definition: Minimum number of second-dose vaccines required

objective.description: "Minimize the total amount of gelatine used in producing the first-dose and second-dose vaccines"

constraints.description: 30 * (number of first-dose vaccines) + 65 * (number of second-dose vaccines) ≤ TotalAntibiotics
The number of first-dose vaccines manufactured must be greater than or equal to the number of second-dose vaccines manufactured
The number of second-dose vaccines manufactured must be at least MinimumSecondDose
